newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's Muoi reaches out to ethnic minorities.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's Muoi reaches out to ethnic minorities.

text.p: Vietnam's Communist Party chief has called for a drive to alleviate poverty and hunger among ethnic minorities who scratch out a meagre living in remote mountainous areas, official media reports said on Wednesday.

In a speech to representatives of the country's 54 ethnic minority groups on Tuesday, Secretary General Do Muoi praised the fortitude of the minorities and said they should be drawn into the fabric of the nation.
"You should direct all your activities to help people of the ethnic groups overcome difficulties and hardships so that they can join the lowland people in building the nation," he said.
Ten years of market reforms and a more open door to the outside world have brought a leap in living standards in Vietnam.
However, more than half of the country's 75 million people still live below an internationally recognised poverty line.
Among those most affected by a lack of clean water, health care and food are women, children and ethnic minorities, who account for 13 percent of the population.

"Ethnic minorities, almost all of whom live in remote areas, are the poorest of the poor, suffering from food shortages for about three to four months of the year," the United Nations Development Programme said in a recent report.

Vietnam has one of the most complex ethno-linguistic mixes in Asia. Its 54 minority groups, many of whom are related to hill tribes of Thailand and Laos, live mostly in the central highlands and mountainous areas in the north.
In addition to physical isolation, ethnic minorities suffer from educational and cultural isolation and are vulnerable to exploitation when they come into contact with the Kinh majority.
The daily Vietnam News quoted Muoi as saying the party and government had, to some extent, neglected the mountainous regions, thereby prolonging the suffering of the indigenous people.

Referring to the beginning of Vietnam's struggle against its French colonialists 50 years ago this week, he praised the ethnic minorities for their "great and glorious contributions" to the revolution.
